findings.evidence: “This skill is a Process … executed with Tool-level rigor” names rubric categories the agent does not need to perform the task. The useful instruction is the factory-subcommand rule and its explanation of delayed failures.
findings.fix: Keep the step sequence, factory-subcommand rule and failure rationale in the introduction. Remove only the rubric labels and record that removal.

findings.evidence: “Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup” misses users who simply ask which reviewers work or why an OpenCode provider no longer appears. “Migrates an old review-spec.toml on first use” also misstates the migrate-only branch, which reports pending migration. The description does not rule out running an already-configured review or execution.
findings.fix: Use when asked to set up or refresh ai-kit cross-AI reviewers or coding executors, pick models from installed CLIs, change the full lane roster or its role orders, check which reviewers are available without saving, diagnose a missing OpenCode provider, or check what happens to an old review-spec.toml. Also use when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers setup because no lanes exist. Proposes review and execute sets, confirms the owner's choices, and writes [lanes] in .aikit/config.toml by default. --local and --global select the target, not permission to replace an existing roster. --check-only saves no config or cache; migration-only reports pending without writing. Not for running an already-configured review or execution, or for an isolated manual config edit.

findings.evidence: “Build the JSON shape … Each object in lanes carries” begins the full write schema and report procedure in the always-loaded body. The body is under 500 lines but has over 6,000 words before any reference is loaded, including write details that headless and check-only runs never use.
findings.fix: Move the complete writer schema, command templates and report examples into a write-and-report reference loaded only on reaching Step 3. Keep the announced-target rule, replacement gate, and exit-status and trust checkpoints in the main flow.

findings.evidence: “Loaded from wizard-flow.md step 2 only” conflicts with SKILL.md line 170 and wizard-flow.md line 50, which also send every kept lane to item 6 for the code-index check.
findings.fix: State both loading triggers in the reference header: items 1–4 for missing listings or unmatched candidates, and item 6 for the kept-lane code-index check. For the latter, direct the agent to item 6 only.

findings.evidence: “First tell the owner that copilot will start in a herdr pane with its permission prompts off … then run” treats notice as consent. With HERDR_ENV=1, the command can start a write-capable CLI before runtime preference or a write-risk answer, even if the owner would not choose Copilot.
findings.fix: Limit interactive Copilot discovery to an owner-selected runtime and require explicit consent before launching it. Default to skipping the pane and use the existing owner-supplied model ID or auto fallback.

findings.evidence: “If the proposal shows an alias group” makes the assertion pass when a regression omits the alias entirely. The input supplies a lane excerpt, but the eval does not control discovery or require that the alias reach the proposal.
findings.fix: Provide a fixture that deterministically exposes the configured router alias to the proposal. Require the alias row to appear in the unranked group with the printed assumption label, and require that no heuristic question be asked.

findings.evidence: The set has 10 positives and 10 negatives, but negatives such as “Write a unit test for the parser in the markdown-to-pdf skill” do not test the activation boundary. Most positives explicitly say review, reviewers or lanes.
findings.fix: Replace the unrelated negative prompts with near misses such as inspecting installed models without configuring ai-kit. Add an implicit positive such as asking which assistant should critique plans and which should implement them, with a separate fallback order for each.

findings.evidence: “Settle Step 2.1's write target and replacement gate before this step” authorizes only the selected target. The catalog fetch calls the merged roster resolver with migration enabled when an installed runtime has no listing. Choosing a new local roster to leave a pending global roster alone can still migrate and retire the global file.
findings.fix: Have catalog discovery resolve candidate rosters without migrating either layer. Leave migration to the explicitly approved target write; until discovery is read-only, do not run that fetch when it would migrate an unapproved layer.

findings.evidence: “One JSON line per project entry that runs as a subprocess … [with] the exact argument list dispatch would run” contradicts the preview implementation. It uses the flattened reviewer view, which can omit an execute entry sharing a review key, and table-runtime previews use the review invocation even for execute-only entries. The owner can be asked to trust a custom execute command that was never shown.
findings.fix: Make the trust preview enumerate effective entries by role and render each role's actual invocation. Ask for trust only after every command-bearing entry has an inspectable argv; if the installed helper cannot show one, report the gap and leave the file untrusted.

findings.evidence: “The innermost one wins” overstates detect-current-runtime. The implementation checks environment markers in fixed priority order; it explicitly does not determine the immediate parent. When both pi and Claude markers remain present, it returns pi even if Claude was launched last.
findings.fix: Describe the result as the first matching host marker in the listed precedence, not as verified nesting. If the owner says the result disagrees with the active host, explain the mismatch and offer an unpinned session-default lane rather than a host-specific alias.

findings.evidence: “Read the vendor's own documentation page for that model or provider” permits a provider-wide page, and line 14 permits third-party reports; SKILL.md line 172 instead requires a page that names the exact model and says to use unknown with source none otherwise. A general retention statement can thus be shown as verified for a model that has different terms.
findings.fix: Use one rule in both places: read the vendor's current documentation for the exact model, label it verified only when it covers that model, and otherwise show unknown with source none. Keep the owner's explicit decision after the note and before any lane test.

findings.evidence: “Codex has no models/list-models subcommand (confirmed via codex --help)” records an undated past check of a version-sensitive CLI surface. The official source confirms debug models exists but does not make the negative claim stable across releases.
findings.fix: Route selection through the current detect-runtimes result and its existing no-list fallback. If retaining the negative CLI claim, make it conditional on the installed binary's current help or cite the official source and date for the specific version checked.
